items.q: In fact, that's where I first heard the great Sid Catlett... And I never will forget, when I entered the door, I could feel the pulsation from those drums, Sid Catlett...

ctx.x: plenty high enough, because you're down there with the people, and people on both sides of you and in front of you -- you're surrounded! So it was a warm feeling. You know, you were really communicating. And it wasn't too big. And the sound was good, everything...

In fact, that's where I first heard the great Sid Catlett. While we were playing at the Club Alabam, we were playing for the big production and we were doing our thing. Melvin White... We also had another fine singer named Estelle Edmonson(?) with the band. And on my break, I walked down to the Downbeat, and Sid Catlett was playing the drums in the Downbeat. They had a very fine tenor player with them. His name was Allan Eager. He eventually went into race-car driving and a whole lot of other things. But they had…

And I never will forget, when I entered the door, I could feel the pulsation from those drums, Sid Catlett... And it was something. Like, the beat met you at the door! And it was not loud. It was just plush. He was a big man with finesse, you know. He had plenty of finesse, and was very high on his instrument, you know.
